question.text: What percentage of the EU hen flock will be sexed with in-ovo sexing technology in Q1 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of the EU's commercial layer hen flock that was sexed with in-ovo technology according to official the first such non-preliminary number published by Innovate Animal Ag in 2027.
question.fine_print: If Innovate Animal Ag does not publish any such number in 2027 or if the criteria are significantly changed such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question can be resolved by another credible source if it is comparable. Otherwise the question will be **annulled**.

research:
I have enough to write this up. Here is what I found.

## 1. Resolution source
- **2026-07 ("Updated July 2026"; data as of 2026-06-01):** Innovate Animal Ag (IAA) puts in-ovo sexing at **40%** of the EU commercial layer flock, with a range of 36.2 to 43.3%. That is about 125 to 142 million hens sexed in-ovo out of about 328 to 346 million commercial hens. When I read the page directly it did not call the figure preliminary. It calls it a base case with uncertainty. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- **The denominator has changed.** Older reports used about 393 to 400 million total hens. The new one uses commercial hens only: 401 million registered places, adjusted for 81.9 to 86% utilisation, with about 42 million backyard hens excluded. Earlier numbers were revised upward on this basis: April 2024 went from 20% to 23%, and April 2025 went from 28% to 34%. The question's background quotes the old 28%. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- **Report timing so far:** the Q1 2024 snapshot was published 2024-07-15, the Q1 2025 snapshot in May 2025, and the June 2026 snapshot in July 2026. The 2027 report could come out around May to July 2027. That may be after the question's resolution date (about 2027-05-31), and its snapshot may be dated mid-2027 rather than Q1. [IAA 2024](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu), [IAA recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No 2027 figure exists. The latest value is 40% (June 2026, new method).
- There is a resolution risk. "The first non-preliminary number published in 2027" could be a revised 2026 figure or a new 2027 snapshot, and the date it describes is uncertain. If the snapshot comes out later than Q1 2027, it would likely include more of the effect of Italy's ban.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- **2026-09-09:** AgFunderNews repeats the 40% figure. Italy plans to phase out culling by 2027. AAT's CEO questions whether Italian producers will import cheaper chicks from countries that still cull. SanOvo/MatrixSpec plan a launch in late 2026 or early 2027. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- **2026-07:** The Commission's Livestock Strategy commits to revising the laying hen rules by end-2026, including ending the systematic killing of male chicks. It is not yet law. [Animal Equality](https://animalequality.org.uk/news/2026/07/08/the-european-commission-includes-plans-to-phase-out-cages-and-end-the-killing-of-male-chicks-in-its-livestock-strategy/), [Brussels Times](https://www.brusselstimes.com/eu-affairs/2227453/eus-new-livestock-strategy-prioritizes-competitiveness-amid-animal-welfare-concerns/)
- **2026 Q2:** IAA's quarterly roundup covers Australia's first adoption and NestFresh's flock being fully in-ovo sexed (both outside the EU). I found no Q3 2026 roundup. [IAA Q2 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q2-2026)
- **Late 2025:** Italy published hatchery guidelines requiring sex determination by day 14 of incubation, with the ban taking effect 2027-01-01. Sources describe the date as subject to possible extensions. [Food Times](https://www.foodtimes.eu/food-system/killing-of-male-chicks-banned-in-italy-only-starting-from-2027/), [Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/male-chicks-killed-birth-ready-guidelines-stop-2027-AHKkAif)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- **Values on the old denominator:** 15% at end Q3 2023, 20% at Q1 2024, 28% at Q1 2025, roughly 8 points a year. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-reaches-15-penetration-in-eu-as-tech-to-end-male-chick-culling-advances), [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu)
- **Values on the new commercial denominator:** 23% (April 2024), 34% (April 2025), 40% (June 2026). Growth was +11 points, then about +6 points over 14 months, so it is slowing.
- **IAA's own forecast:** about 51% by July 2028 (range 47 to 55%), roughly +5.5 points a year. Straight-line interpolation (my arithmetic, not an IAA figure) gives about 42 to 43% for Q1 2027 and about 45% for mid-2027. IAA expects Italy's ban to phase in over about 18 months, and warns adoption could saturate without an EU-wide mandate. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- **Revisions:** both earlier figures were later revised upward, by 3 and 6 points, mostly because the denominator changed.
- **Seasonality:** the figure is a stock of hens on farms, so seasonality is not a meaningful factor. Hen flocks turn over in roughly 18-month cycles, which slows how quickly new placements show up in the share.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the markets in the provided feed match this question. The Flock-camera, EU budget and market-share contracts are all unrelated. I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on in-ovo penetration.
- The only expert forecast I found is IAA's 51% by July 2028.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **2027-01-01:** Italy's ban takes effect. Italy kills about 30 million male chicks a year. Watch for delays or a shift to imported chicks.
- **By end-2026:** a possible Commission proposal to revise the laying hen rules. A proposal is not law and would not change Q1 2027 numbers, but it could drive adoption ahead of a mandate.
- **Late 2026 or early 2027:** SanOvo/MatrixSpec launch, adding capacity.
- **Q4 2026 to Q1 2027:** IAA quarterly roundups and a 2026 yearly recap (last year's came out 2026-01-04). These might restate figures.
- **About May to July 2027:** IAA's annual penetration report, the likely resolution number. It may come after 2027-05-31, so check the publication timing.
- **Ongoing:** avian influenza in the EU and UK in November 2026 could disrupt placements and hatcheries. Weather is not otherwise relevant.

I've finished the research and am writing up the findings. The main points: the latest official number is 40% (June 1, 2026), and the next annual report may only come out mid-2027.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (page updated July 2026): Innovate Animal Ag's (IAA) Market Penetration and Forecast page says **40% of the EU commercial layer flock was in-ovo sexed as of June 1, 2026**, with a range of 36.2% to 43.3%. That is about 130M of roughly 340M hens. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- The same page revises earlier figures because the flock-size estimate changed. The denominator is now 328M to 346M hens, down from 393M:
  - April 1, 2024: 23% (was 20%)
  - April 1, 2025: 34% (was 28%)
  - IAA forecasts about 51% (range 47% to 55%) by July 2028, assuming Italy's ban starts January 2027 as planned. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Method: over 90% of the data is self-reported by suppliers. The window is the past 18 months, matching one layer cycle. The page does not label any figure "preliminary". [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- **Timing risk:** the snapshot dates and publication dates have moved around:
  - Q1 2024 figure: published 2024-07-15 [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu)
  - Q1 2025 figure: published 2025-05-15 [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/2025-in-ovo-sexing-market-penetration-and-forecast-report)
  - June 1, 2026 figure: published July 2026
  - The 2027 report could therefore measure mid-2027 rather than Q1 2027, and could come out after the 2027-05-31 resolution date. It is unclear how the question would treat that.
- **Comparability:** the question background uses the old 393M base, which gave 28% for 2025. The revised series gives 34% for the same date. If the question is judged on the new series, the starting points are about 6 points higher.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No 2027 figure exists. The latest official value is 40% as of 2026-06-01.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10: There is still no EU-wide ban on chick culling. A coalition says leaked Commission drafts include one, but I could not confirm this. [Wikipedia summary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_culling)
- 2026-09-09, AgFunder reporting on the 40% figure:
  - Switzerland is above 85% and Norway at 52%.
  - In Ovo, once a well-funded sector leader, has left the market.
  - Italy's ban could be undercut by importing chicks from hatcheries that cull males.
  - The Dutch industry has pledged to use in-ovo sexing by July 2027.
  - [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- 2026-07-07: The Commission's Livestock Strategy (COM(2026) 576) says it intends to propose revised welfare rules for laying hens and broilers by end-2026, including an end to the systematic killing of male chicks. [Animal Equality](https://animalequality.org.uk/news/2026/07/08/the-european-commission-includes-plans-to-phase-out-cages-and-end-the-killing-of-male-chicks-in-its-livestock-strategy/)
- 2026 (Q2 roundup): covers Australia, NestFresh and Hitachi, with no new EU numbers. [IAA Q2 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q2-2026)
- 2026-03-31 (Q1 roundup): lists Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland, the Netherlands and Norway as "transitioning fully". [IAA Q1 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q1-2026)
- Italy's ban applies from 2027-01-01 (Legislative Decree 205/2023). Guidelines are reportedly ready. [Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/male-chicks-killed-birth-ready-guidelines-stop-2027-AHKkAif)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- **Old series** (roughly 393M to 400M denominator):
  - End Q3 2023: 15%
  - End Q1 2024: 20%
  - End Q1 2025: 28% (+8 points in a year)
  - [IAA 2024](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-has-now-hit-20-of-the-market-in-the-eu), [IAA 2025](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/2025-in-ovo-sexing-market-penetration-and-forecast-report)
- **Revised series** (about 340M denominator):
  - April 2024: 23%
  - April 2025: 34% (+11 points)
  - June 2026: 40% (+6 points in 14 months, about 0.43 points a month)
  - Growth is slowing as the countries with bans approach saturation.
- **Simple extrapolations (arithmetic only, not a forecast):**
  - Continuing the latest pace from June 2026 to about April 1, 2027 gives roughly 44%.
  - IAA's own path from 40% (June 2026) to 51% (July 2028) is about 0.44 points a month, which gives about 44% for Q1 2027 and about 45% to 46% for mid-2027.
- **Year-on-year change:** recent annual gains are 5 to 11 points. Revisions to past figures have been as large as +6 points.
- **Seasonality:** none to speak of. Each figure covers an 18-month window, so it changes slowly.

## 5. Other forecasts
- The only expert forecast I found is IAA's own: about 51% (47% to 55%) by July 2028.
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied are relevant. They cover Flock cameras, EU budget and tariffs, AI market share and so on. I found no Manifold or Metaculus market on this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **End-2026:** the Commission's planned proposal on laying hens and broilers, which may include an EU-wide ban on chick culling. A proposal would not force adoption before Q1 2027, but it could lead to some hatcheries switching early.
- **2027-01-01:** Italy's ban takes effect. Hatchery output switches straight away, but the flock turns over across roughly 18 months, so the effect builds slowly.
- **Through July 2027:** the Dutch industry's in-ovo pledge deadline. Norway's industry target is 2027-07-01, but Norway is outside the EU.
- **Next IAA reports:** a Q3 2026 roundup (not yet published), a 2026 annual recap (likely early January 2027), and the 2027 market penetration report. Going by past years, that report would come out between mid-May and July 2027, possibly after the resolution date.
- **Risks:** supply side, after In Ovo's exit, and whether the flock-size or method revisions happen again.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The forecast window closes on 2026-12-31. The resolving figure will probably come from IAA's annual report, which is likely published between May and July 2027. That is about 6 to 8 months from now. It could land after the nominal 2027-05-31 resolution date.

(b) **Latest known value:** 40% of the EU commercial layer flock, range 36.2 to 43.3%. This is IAA's figure for data as of 2026-06-01, published in July 2026, and it uses the new commercial-only denominator.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 40%.

(d) **If the trend continued:** On the new denominator the series went 23% (April 2024), 34% (April 2025) and 40% (June 2026). Growth is slowing. IAA forecasts about 51% by July 2028, which works out to roughly 5.5 points a year. Interpolating gives about 42 to 43% for Q1 2027 and about 44 to 45% for a mid-2027 snapshot. Italy's ban starts 2027-01-01 and should add something, but flock turnover is slow, so only about 1 to 2 points by mid-2027.

(e) **Historical variation:** Year-over-year changes have been 6 to 11 points. Past figures were revised by 3 to 6 points, mainly because the denominator changed. There is also a definitional risk: the snapshot date (Q1 versus mid-2027) and the denominator method could each shift the result by a few points.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** IAA's own trajectory implies about 42 to 46% around Q1 to mid-2027. No prediction markets cover this question.

(g) **Scenarios:**
- **Low outcome:** Several things could pull the figure down:
  - Italy delays its ban, or its producers import culled-sex chicks.
  - Avian influenza disrupts placements.
  - Saturation sets in without an EU-wide mandate.
  - A resolver falls back on the old total-hen denominator, which would give a figure in the mid-30s.
- **High outcome:** Three things together could push the figure up:
  - The snapshot is dated mid-to-late 2027.
  - Italian, Spanish or Polish adoption accelerates ahead of the Commission's proposal.
  - New capacity from SanOvo/MatrixSpec comes online.

  Together these could push the figure to around 50% or higher.

**Tails:**
- **1st percentile, about 33:** an old-denominator comparable figure, or a downward revision combined with stalled adoption.
- **99th percentile, about 55:** a late-2027 snapshot combined with a strong Italian uptake.

(f) Experts and markets: IAA's base case is about 51% by July 2028, which implies about 44 to 45% in mid-2027. There are no relevant prediction markets.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:

- High outcome: Italy implements fully and fast, new capacity from SanOvo/MatrixSpec and others arrives, producers act early on the Commission's pledge to end chick culling, and a mid-2027 snapshot date captures more of this. The result could be 50% or more.
